plans.note: Section 7 expressly covers limitations of liability; check whether the cap is mutual, tied to a meaningful multiple of fees, and whether carve-outs (IP indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) exist.

Heading of Section 7 is 'Indemnification of Contractor' only, so a vendor-to-customer indemnity for third-party IP claims and Contractor misconduct appears absent; add it in Section 7 and narrow our reverse indemnity.
No covenants/restrictive-covenant section in the outline; scan the purpose-of-engagement language in Section 1 for any restraint on our business or competing purchases before concluding it is absent.
No exclusivity section appears; Section 1 (purpose/scope) is the only plausible home for sole-source or exclusive-engagement wording.
Pricing sits in Section 3 (Contractor's Compensation); check there for any best-pricing or favoured-terms obligation running against us — none is signalled by the outline.
No personnel or covenants section listed; if a non-solicit exists it would likely be tucked into the engagement terms (Section 1) or survival language in Section 6.
Section 6 (Termination) governs; confirm we hold convenience termination on short notice without penalty and that Contractor cannot terminate mid-engagement for convenience.
No separate term section is listed; term/renewal mechanics, if any, would sit in Section 6 — check for auto-renewal, notice window and uncapped renewal pricing.
No general/miscellaneous section appears in the outline (Section 2 is not listed); verify the tail of the agreement for governing law and venue and add an approved-law clause if truly missing.
No assignment/miscellaneous section listed; check Section 6 and any unlisted boilerplate for anti-assignment or change-of-control termination rights.

Section 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) is the operative clause; confirm work product and our data vest in us and that no back-assignment or licence of our IP runs to Contractor.
Any licence-back or retained-tools licence should appear in Section 4; test scope for affiliate and contractor use and remove any at-will revocability.
No audit or records section listed; check compensation (Section 3) for inspection-of-records rights running against us before treating as absent.
Look for penalty, late-fee or liquidated-damages amounts payable by us in Sections 3 and 7; the outline suggests none, but interest on late payment may be lurking in Section 3.
Section 5 pairs Contractor warranties with a disclaimer; confirm a services/conformity-to-Specifications warranty of meaningful duration and a repair-or-refund remedy survive the disclaimer.

No insurance section appears; propose standard coverages (CGL, professional liability/E&O, cyber, workers' comp) alongside the Contractor covenants in Section 5 given Contractor handles our materials.
Check Section 3 for minimum fees, retainer floors or take-or-pay commitments; none is flagged in the outline, but compensation terms are the likely location.
Section 6 addresses termination but the outline shows no wind-down obligations; add transition assistance and return/deletion of our materials, cross-referencing ownership in Section 4.
